author: cushag
text:
“He” had always been so fond of me.

“She” never seemed to like me much at all.

But “he,” oh, how we loved one another!

It is time we were off, mother!
Let us go and fetch them back,
With their red eyes full of fire.
Mother, I will not be tricked,
Or I shall weep for ever.
Come away now or we shall die!

These are very simple pieces from children—a story and some lines about death. They seem to me delightful bits of art, and worth considering as such by persons who read much poetry but care little about prose. I have been reading in the newspaper that a man named Robert Burns died this morning. He was quite young; he died unmarried and without children; and as far as we know, left no relatives or friends to regret his death, except perhaps some who owe him money, but they probably will not miss him. It would be difficult to say what may become of him now. His body must be buried somewhere, but there is no doubt that he will go where people do not think much about them. Me name's Polly Ann, An' that's all my friends know.

I never had any other name but so;

My father and mother were both named Polly Ann.

author: emily_dickinson

Here is a song for thee:
 One single bird has sung it;
 One only voice hath sung it,
 As if one little thing had done it, —
 As though a tiny bee,
 A bumblebee or a butterfly
 Had made it with its wings.

The sun in all its glory sets;
Night comes on apace, and darkness spreads:
In the garden walks no glimmer breaks,
Save such as we from our candles make.

There is no beauty like that which one sees
In the clear stream from Heaven descending fair;
The purest stream that flows beneath the sky's vault
Softer than women's voices in their prayer
Is its silver flow when it hastens down.

"At my school they said I had a genius mind,
So I ran away to sea at fifteen-nine.
My first voyage ended in an African war,
Where I killed many men and saw more die.
Then home for leave, where she knew what I could do;
She gave me good advice but let me go.
Two years again in Africa, now for China."

The world is not so big that I cannot live in it

without its being turned round for me.

He who has been born under the sun should not cry

Alas for wretchedness! but rather, Rejoice in this life,

For all things are good, though little or much;

Be thankful to God above and below that thou art,

And enjoy the present time as it comes along.

I saw him on the sands sit down at noon;

All covered o'er with dust and bloody wounds,

And from the sunshade in his hand took some cool water,

With which he washed his eyes and forehead, though,

By reason of his pain, he could not drink it up.

But I perceived that he did this for sport.

Are yours? How much you do! How many needs
Have you beside your own?" He added further,
Looking down upon me,—'tis a common trick—
That I should give too much away.

author: robert_frost
text: "My poor old horse died last night; he'd been ailing long enough, but you know how we are, always giving them more than they want. It never seems much in your head till you get down on the ground and pull the plug out, then you begin to feel bad about it. But anyway he went without a struggle, which wasn't so bad. Well, he'll lie here all day under this big tree, while everybody talks over their troubles, and nobody remembers him except me."

author: stothert_james_a
text:
To me at morn my eyes are turned, and pray
For thee ; for thou art mine, from whom I draw
My life : 'tis sweet to gaze upon thy face;
No other sun does give so bright a ray,
As thine, which makes the world rejoice with glee,
So glorious, fair, and radiant, yet so free.

text:
The stars have ceased to hide themselves
 From out their golden crown of blue,
 Yet still they seem too far off for eyes
 That know not what they look upon!
 In vain I seek my dreams, alas!
 While down the western path they pass,
 Where only yesterday I saw them shine!

 The day that was my friend!
 Yet, all I did today has been undone,
 For what have I gained?

THE morning came, we woke, we went,
We sought, but found not, that spot of green
Where were the flowers, songs, birds, and things.
That other world had vanished then.

And after another day or two:

THERE is one thing I know about me—I am an idealist!
